# The tempura timeline language

Every form, key and value kind of the `(timeline …)` vocabulary, rendered from
`schema/tempura.sjon`'s own `:description`s. The manifest is the single source:
edit it, run `zig build docs`, and review the diff — `zig build verify` fails
when the page and the manifest disagree.

What is here is what one form can say about itself. The rules that are relations
BETWEEN forms — document order, an anchor's digest, a bound lane's address, two
notes overlapping on one key — are tempura's own diagnostics, and
[`docs/plans/02-timeline-schema.md`](plans/02-timeline-schema.md) is where they
are written down.

The hosted `midi/` and `it/` tiers (`schema/midi.sjon`, `schema/it.sjon`) and
the verbatim pacer copy (`schema/pacer.sjon`) are separate vocabularies with
their own references; only the timeline tier is rendered here.

## Forms

### `(timeline …)`

The document's header: what the piece is called, how long it is, what happens at the end, and which anchor conducts it. One per document, first — a second is a tempura timeline_duplicate with its own span, since a head-set counts a form's children and not a document's roots.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:title` | `string` | no | — | The piece's title. Prose, not an identifier. |
| `:length` | `number+unit` | no | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>The piece's length. Omitted, it is the end of the last event or clip rounded up to a bar. |
| `:fps` | `frame-rate-scalar \| frame-rate-pair` | no | — | integer; min 1; max 16777215; len 2; integer; min 1; max 16777215<br>The document's frame rate, for the `f` position unit (plan 03): frames per second as an integer (`:fps 25`) or an exact rational (`:fps [30000 1001]`). Never a bare decimal — 29.97 would mean 2997/100, and NTSC is 30000/1001. A rate alone changes no position's spelling; the header keeps `:fps`. An `f` position without this key is a tempura frame_rate_missing. |
| `:end` | `symbol enum` | no | `hold` | one of: `loop`, `hold`<br>What the playhead does past :length. Exported as pacer's transport :end. |
| `:conductor` | `ref → (anchor :id …)` | no | — | The anchor whose tempo and meter conduct this document (plan 03, "Three conductors"). With one, the document's own (tempo-point …) and (meter-point …) forms are a conductor_conflict; without one, a tempo point and a meter point at tick 0 are required. |

### `(anchor …)`

A file this document is arranged around — the it set's (source …) generalised to both formats. An anchor is BY REFERENCE when the document holds no dump for it and INLINE when a (midi/smf …) or (it/module …) root follows it. The pairing is POSITIONAL and one dump per anchor, which is document order and therefore not a shape this form can carry: a dump with no anchor before it is anchor_missing, a second dump for one anchor is anchor_dump_duplicate, and a hosted (it/source …) inside an inline module that disagrees with the anchor is anchor_conflict.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:id` | `symbol` | yes | — | This anchor's name, referenced by :conductor and by a bound lane's :from. |
| `:kind` | `symbol enum` | yes | — | one of: `smf`, `it`<br>Which format the file is. |
| `:file` | `string` | yes | — | Path to the file, resolved relative to this document. |
| `:size` | `number` | no | — | integer; min 0<br>The file's length in bytes. Checked with :sha256 before any offset into the file is honoured; a disagreement is anchor_mismatch, never a silent re-read. |
| `:sha256` | `string` | no | — | Hex digest of the file's bytes, checked with :size. |

### `(tempo-point …)`

A tempo change: from :at onward the piece runs at this tempo, until the next tempo point or the end. Tempo is a step function — a source that slides yields one point per tick and coalescing happens at export. Strictly ascending in document order (tempo_map_invalid), and one at tick 0 is required when the document has no :conductor. This form is the ONLY way a timeline document says tempo: a pass-through pacer (transport …) or (tempo …) is passthrough_conducts, because tempura emits those itself at export.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:at` | `number+unit` | yes | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`<br>Where the segment starts. Never in seconds: seconds are what this map defines. |
| `:us` | `number` | no | — | integer; min 1; max 16777215<br>Microseconds per quarter note — an SMF file's own field. Exclusive with :qpm. |
| `:qpm` | `number` | no | — | min 1; max 1000<br>Quarter notes per minute. Exclusive with :us. |

Exclusive group (exactly_one): `:us` | `:qpm`.

### `(meter-point …)`

A meter change. Each must sit on a bar line of the meter before it (meter_off_bar) — a meter change mid-bar is not a thing in any source format — and one at tick 0 is required when the document has no :conductor.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:at` | `number+unit` | yes | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`<br>Where the meter changes. Never in seconds. |
| `:sig` | `vector<number>` | yes | — | len 2; integer; min 1; max 64<br>The time signature from :at onward, as [n d]. |

### `(section …)`

A named window on the timeline, exported as a pacer (scene …) of the same name. Sections may overlap; a (scene …) passing through under a name a section also uses is scene_duplicate.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:name` | `symbol` | yes | — | The window's name, unique per document. |
| `:at` | `number+unit` | yes | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>Where the window opens. |
| `:dur` | `number+unit` | yes | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>How long the window lasts. |

### `(cue …)`

A named point in time — never a window. SMF markers and cue points dump to cues; pacer gets a comment, since a point has no scene.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:name` | `string` | yes | — | What the point is called. Prose: SMF marker text is arbitrary bytes. |
| `:at` | `number+unit` | yes | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>Where the point sits. |

### `(lane …)`

One stream of content driving one pacer target. :kind is the discriminant and decides which keys exist and what the children mean. A lane is NATIVE when it carries content and BOUND when it names an anchor with :from — never both (bound_lane_has_content), and content has one home.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:name` | `symbol` | yes | — | This lane's name, unique across the timeline's lanes. |
| `:kind` | `symbol enum` | no | `notes` | one of: `notes`, `curve`, `query`, `formula`<br>What this lane carries, and the discriminant that gates the keys below. Write it BEFORE them. |
| `:target` | `symbol` | no | — | The pacer name this lane drives at export. Defaults to :name. |
| `:from` | `ref → (anchor :id …)` | no | — | The anchor this lane reads its content from. A lane with :from is BOUND: its content lives in the file, and children here are bound_lane_has_content. Only a notes or curve lane may bind — a query or formula lane that names one is bound_kind_invalid, which is a relation between :kind and :from and so cannot be a variant gate. |
| `:track` | `number` | no | — | integer; min 1<br>Which track of a bound SMF anchor, 1-based in file order. |
| `:ch` | `midi-channel \| midi-channel-set` | no | — | integer; min 1; max 16; min-len 1; max-len 16; integer; min 1; max 16<br>Which MIDI channel of a bound SMF anchor, 1..16 — or which channels, as a vector: `:ch [1 2]` reads both channels of the one :track. The vector is what a dump writes when a native lane whose notes named several channels comes back bound (residue rule 2: the lane binds at its track and at every channel its records name). A native lane's notes carry their own :ch and take none from the lane's (the lane's is a binding key); a vector on a native lane is address_invalid. |
| `:channel` | `number` | no | — | integer; min 1; max 64<br>Which channel of a bound Impulse Tracker anchor, 1..64. |

Positional children: `form: (note …, local) | (keyframe …, local) | (clip …, local)`.

#### `(note …)`

A note event. Two notes on one key overlapping in one lane are note_overlap.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:at` | `number+unit` | yes | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>The onset. |
| `:dur` | `number+unit` | yes | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>How long the note sounds, measured from :at. |
| `:key` | `note-key-number \| note-key-name` | yes | — | integer; min 0; max 127<br>Which key: the MIDI number, or the note name. |
| `:vel` | `number` | no | `100` | integer; min 1; max 127; repr f32<br>On-velocity. |
| `:ch` | `number` | no | — | integer; min 1; max 16<br>MIDI channel for rendering. Defaults to 1. A lane's own :ch is a BINDING key — which channels of a bound anchor the lane reads — and says nothing about the notes a native lane carries, so it is not the default here (a ruling `doc/fromSjon.zig` records at `default_note_ch`). |
| `:off-vel` | `number` | no | — | integer; min 0; max 127<br>Off-velocity. MIDI rendering only. |

#### `(keyframe …)`

A value reached exactly at :at, with the easing that shaped the segment ENDING here. Before the first keyframe the lane holds its first value; after the last, its last. A curve is NAMED, never drawn — pacer's rule, so there are no Theatre-style handles.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:at` | `number+unit` | yes | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>Where the value lands. |
| `:value` | `key-scalar \| key-vector` | yes | — | repr f32; min-len 1; max-len 4; repr f32<br>The value reached at :at: a scalar or a 1-4 component vector. |
| `:ease` | `ease-name \| ease-form` | no | `linear` | one of: `linear`, `hold`, `smoothstep`, `in-quad`, `out-quad`, `in-out-quad`, `in-cubic`, `out-cubic`, `in-out-cubic`, `in-quart`, `out-quart`, `in-out-quart`, `in-sine`, `out-sine`, `in-out-sine`, `in-expo`, `out-expo`, `in-out-expo`<br>The easing over the segment ending at this keyframe: a pacer easing name (in-cubic, hold, …) or a pacer easing form ((spring …), (steps …), (cubic-bezier …), (seq …), (chain …)). Typed by pacer's OWN kind, so the two vocabularies cannot drift. |

#### `(clip …)`

A phrase placed on this lane. It places the phrase's lane of the same :name as this lane; a phrase with no such lane is clip_lane_missing.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:at` | `number+unit` | yes | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>Where the phrase starts. |
| `:phrase` | `ref → (phrase :name …)` | yes | — | Which phrase to place. |
| `:repeat` | `number` | no | `1` | integer; min 1<br>How many times the phrase plays. |
| `:offset` | `number+unit` | no | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>Where in the phrase playback begins. Defaults to 0 — a default this manifest cannot declare, because a :default literal is unit-free and dropping the unit off a position would be exactly the silent guess the position kind exists to refuse (pacer says the same of a trigger's :offset). |
| `:length` | `number+unit` | no | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>The playback window measured from :offset. Defaults to the phrase's length times :repeat minus :offset; content past the window is not placed, which is what a split clip's left half needs. |
| `:transpose` | `number` | no | `0` | integer; min -120; max 120<br>Semitones to shift the placed notes by. Notes only. |

### `(phrase …)`

A reusable fragment: lanes with content, placed by a (clip …). A phrase's lanes carry content only — :from inside one is phrase_lane_bound, a clip inside one is clip_nested, and :target is ignored (the placing lane's target applies).

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:name` | `symbol` | yes | — | This phrase's name, referenced by a clip's :phrase. |
| `:length` | `number+unit` | yes | — | unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`<br>The phrase's length. A clip that repeats places one copy per :length. |

## Value kinds

### position

A position or duration on the tick grid: a number carrying a REQUIRED unit — q (quarter notes), t (tempura ticks, TPQ = 46126080 per quarter), bar and b (bars and beats, counted from 0 through the meter map), s (seconds, through the tempo map), or f (frames, through the document's declared :fps rate and the tempo map). A bare number is unit_required, never a guess. A duration (:dur, :length, :offset) is measured from its own form's :at, so an s or f duration resolves at that anchor. Negative positions are a tempura position_negative diagnostic, not a bound here.

Type: `number+unit` — unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`/`s`/`f`.

### grid-position

A position on the tempo and meter maps themselves: q, t, bar or b, never s. Seconds are derived FROM these maps, so a seconds position on the form that defines them is circular — pacer refuses it on (tempo :at …) for the same reason. Never f either — frames are counted through the tempo map, which these forms define.

Type: `number+unit` — unit `q`/`t`/`bar`/`b`.

### timeline-end

What the playhead does past :length. Spelled and meant exactly as pacer's end-behavior, which is what the exported transport carries.

Type: `symbol enum` — one of: `loop`, `hold`.

### anchor-id

An anchor's identifier, and the cross-ref target a :conductor or a bound lane's :from names. Unique per document.

Type: `symbol`.

### anchor-ref

Names an (anchor :id …) declared in this document. A name no anchor declares is not_cross_ref, naming the form it had to be declared by.

Type: `ref → (anchor :id …)`.

### anchor-kind

Which file format an anchor points at. The kind decides which address keys a bound lane may carry — checked host-side as address_invalid, since the schema sees the lane and the anchor one at a time.

Type: `symbol enum` — one of: `smf`, `it`.

### byte-size

A file's length in bytes, as the anchor recorded it. Verified against the file with :sha256 before any (bin …) offset or bound lane is honoured (anchor_mismatch) — never a silent re-read.

Type: `number` — integer; min 0.

### us-per-quarter

Microseconds per quarter note — the SMF set-tempo field, kept in its own spelling so a document imported from a .mid stays exact in text.

Type: `number` — integer; min 1; max 16777215.

### qpm-value

Quarter notes per minute. Fractional tempi are legal; the IT Txx range (32..255) sits inside this one, so a document imported from a .it says :qpm and stays exact.

Type: `number` — min 1; max 1000.

### sig-component

One component of a time signature, integer 1..64. The numerator's real ceiling is 64 and the denominator's is the power-of-two set {1 2 4 8 16 32} — a vector types both its elements alike, so the denominator's shape is a tempura meter_map_invalid with the form's span.

Type: `number` — integer; min 1; max 64.

### meter-sig

A time signature as [beats-per-bar note-value], e.g. [4 4] or [7 8]. A bar is (4 n / d) quarters.

Type: `vector<number>` — len 2; integer; min 1; max 64.

### frame-rate-scalar

A frame rate as whole frames per second, e.g. 25 — the rates film and video count in. Bounded like us-per-quarter, to catch typos; the f unit's arithmetic cannot overflow at any bound.

Type: `number` — integer; min 1; max 16777215.

### frame-rate-pair

A frame rate as an exact [num den] rational, e.g. [30000 1001] for NTSC or [24000 1001] for 23.976 film. Never a bare decimal: 29.97 would mean 2997/100, and NTSC does not.

Type: `vector<number>` — len 2; integer; min 1; max 16777215.

### frame-rate

The document's frame rate for the f position unit (plan 03): an integer or an exact [num den] rational.

Type: `frame-rate-scalar | frame-rate-pair` — integer; min 1; max 16777215; len 2; integer; min 1; max 16777215.

### section-name

A section's identifier: the window's name, unique per document, and the name of the pacer (scene …) it exports to.

Type: `symbol`.

### lane-name

A lane's identifier, unique across the timeline's lanes. A clip places the phrase's lane of the same :name as the placing lane.

Type: `symbol`.

### lane-target

The pacer name this lane drives at export, resolved there against the host registries exactly as a pacer track's :target is. Defaults to the lane's own :name — a default this manifest cannot declare, since it copies another key.

Type: `symbol`.

### phrase-name

A phrase's identifier, and the cross-ref target a clip's :phrase names.

Type: `symbol`.

### phrase-ref

Names a (phrase :name …) declared in this document. A name no phrase declares is not_cross_ref.

Type: `ref → (phrase :name …)`.

### lane-kind

The discriminant: which keys a lane has, and what its content means. Write it BEFORE the keys it enables — a variant key ahead of its discriminant is unknown_key.

Type: `symbol enum` — one of: `notes`, `curve`, `query`, `formula`.

### track-index

Which track of a bound SMF anchor this lane reads, 1-based in file order.

Type: `number` — integer; min 1.

### midi-channel

A MIDI channel, 1..16 as every display counts them (0..15 on the wire).

Type: `number` — integer; min 1; max 16.

### it-channel

An Impulse Tracker channel, 1..64.

Type: `number` — integer; min 1; max 64.

### cc-number

A MIDI controller number, 0..127.

Type: `number` — integer; min 0; max 127.

### cc-pair

A 14-bit controller as [msb lsb] — two controller numbers read as one value.

Type: `vector<number>` — len 2; integer; min 0; max 127.

### cc-address

A controller address: one number for a 7-bit controller, or an [msb lsb] pair for a 14-bit one.

Type: `cc-number | cc-pair` — integer; min 0; max 127; len 2; integer; min 0; max 127.

### midi-channel-set

Several MIDI channels of one track as a vector, [1 2] — each 1..16, and no channel twice (a repeat, or an empty vector, is address_invalid: the manifest bounds the elements and the host checks the set).

Type: `vector<number>` — min-len 1; max-len 16; integer; min 1; max 16.

### midi-channels

Which MIDI channels of one track a bound lane reads: one midi-channel, or a midi-channel-set of several.

Type: `midi-channel | midi-channel-set` — integer; min 1; max 16; min-len 1; max-len 16; integer; min 1; max 16.

### curve-column

Which Impulse Tracker column a bound curve lane reads.

Type: `symbol enum` — one of: `vol`, `pan`, `fx`.

### fx-letter

An Impulse Tracker effect letter, A..Z — the effect whose parameter a bound :column fx lane reads.

Type: `string` — min-len 1; max-len 1.

### range-bound

One end of a bound curve's output range. Narrowed to f32 at export, so it must fit that range.

Type: `number` — repr f32.

### value-range

The [lo hi] a bound curve's normalised value is scaled into at export.

Type: `vector<number>` — len 2; repr f32.

### key-scalar

A unitless keyframe value. Narrowed to f32 at export, pacer's determinism seam, so it must fit that range.

Type: `number` — repr f32.

### key-vector

A 1-4 component keyframe value (vec2 / vec3 / vec4 targets). Arity is joined against the resolved target at export.

Type: `vector<number>` — min-len 1; max-len 4; repr f32.

### keyframe-value

A keyframe's value: a scalar or a 1-4 component vector — pacer's own key-value shape.

Type: `key-scalar | key-vector` — repr f32; min-len 1; max-len 4; repr f32.

### note-key-number

A MIDI key number, 0..127 (60 is middle C).

Type: `number` — integer; min 0; max 127.

### note-key-name

A note name: "C4" is 60, sharps spelled # and flats b, the midi set's middle-C-is-C4 convention. The spelling is checked host-side so a typo names the octave it could not read.

Type: `string`.

### note-key

A key: the MIDI number, or the note name that reads better.

Type: `note-key-number | note-key-name` — integer; min 0; max 127.

### velocity

A note's on-velocity, 1..127. Zero is a note-off on the wire and is never written here. Reaches an f32 lane at export.

Type: `number` — integer; min 1; max 127; repr f32.

### release-velocity

A note's off-velocity, 0..127. MIDI rendering only — nothing else reads it.

Type: `number` — integer; min 0; max 127.

### repeat-count

How many times a clip plays its phrase, at least once.

Type: `number` — integer; min 1.

### transpose-semitones

Semitones a clip shifts the phrase's notes by; ten octaves each way is well past any key range. Notes only — a curve clip ignores it.

Type: `number` — integer; min -120; max 120.

### lane-content

A lane's children: note events, keyframes, and clips of a phrase. Each body is declared LOCAL to (lane …), so none of these three heads exists anywhere else — which is what lets `note` be tempura's timeline event while midivia's `note` verb keeps its own meaning in its own set.

Type: `form: (note …) | (keyframe …) | (clip …)`.

### phrase-section

A phrase's children: one or more (lane …) forms with content only. A phrase with no lane places nothing.

Type: `form: (lane …)`.
